# Scientific Literature Review

Curated by Skill Harbor: a systematic literature-review workflow that turns Muse into a rigorous research assistant instead of a confident summarizer. It starts by converting your prompt into a searchable research question (PICO for clinical work: population, intervention, comparator, outcome; system/method/baseline/metric for technical work), then builds a search protocol before collecting a single source: databases to search, date ranges, languages. Sources are screened explicitly, synthesized across review types (narrative for orientation, scoping for mapping gaps, systematic for publication-grade claims, meta-analysis for quantitative aggregation), with citation checks and an evidence log so every claim traces back to a source. It asks which level of rigor you need and defaults sensibly: scoping for exploration, systematic for publication or clinical claims. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure workflow guidance, nothing to install; the agent can only work with sources it can actually access, verify database access first; a literature review supports your judgment, it does not replace domain expertise or peer review. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
